subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should Slack support an explicit user-account DM mode that receives user-authorized `message.im` events and replies with an xoxp user token, or should OpenClaw keep Slack DM handling bot-identity-only?
rationale: The code path is clear, but choosing whether OpenClaw may act as a regular Slack user identity is a product/security boundary rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Add explicit user-account mode
options.body: Implement a default-off Slack mode with authorization-to-token mapping, user-token reply selection, scope docs, guardrails, and live proof.

options.title: Keep Slack bot-only
options.body: Document that `userToken` remains read-oriented and that natural user-identity DM handling is outside the supported Slack plugin model.

options.title: Require live design proof first
options.body: Ask for a redacted Slack event envelope, exact scopes, and threat model before accepting any implementation.

recommendation.title: Add explicit user-account mode
recommendation.body: Implement a default-off Slack mode with authorization-to-token mapping, user-token reply selection, scope docs, guardrails, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original user-token surface and recent adjacent Slack token work, making him the best available routing owner for the product/security decision.
